top_choice_rationale: Carson (P001) has the most distinctive voice on the shortlist: cool, exact, able to turn suddenly to desire or grief. Her formal invention serves specific emotional and intellectual problems, as in the verse novel Autobiography of Red and the elegy Nox. Her long engagement with Greek and Latin literature works as method, not decoration, and her form keeps changing across verse narrative, lyric, elegy and essay. The citation I support is limited to original written work in English, which answers the scope objections about hybrid or book-object form, translation and scholarship. Her sustained quality beyond the landmark books (the essays, Plainwater, The Beauty of the Husband, Red Doc>, Float) rests on public knowledge and is unverified by me. My confidence may also be inflated because I can judge her English directly and Cărtărescu only in translation. I rank Cărtărescu (P002) second: his single developing project is a serious oeuvre-level claim, but I cannot settle from translations whether his recurring imagery is development or repetition. No award (P000) is last, since both substantive proposals meet the common criteria well enough to be preferred.
